item: Design a third VerificationState for the setback extraction acceptance gate (gate.ts), covering values read from a real primary source but never round-tripped against a code-section atom corpus. Originated from Belton's research agent hitting 254 G2 blocks.
checkpoint: DONE. legacy-design-tools PR #628 merged to main (e503756b), branch deleted.

whatShipped.newState: VerificationState 'primary-source-verified', adopted from a reference design cente-67 (Engine) built independently and shared -- reviewed their actual gate.ts diff and test file directly before adopting, not just the description. atom_did made optional and omitted entirely for this state (a fake-looking convention ID, not an honest omission, is what actually trips G2's fabricated-citation block). G2 emits an explicit PASS-level result with a clear reason for this state. G5 (quote round-trip) skipped -- no atom body exists to check against. G1/G3/G4/G6 unchanged and still apply.
whatShipped.elginFix: Separate commit fixing a real defect in the earlier Elgin port (PR #627): its verification_state 'transcribed' was never a valid value in gate.ts's type at all (strictly asserted|human-verified before this PR) -- would BLOCK G6 the first time anyone ran the gate against it. Confirmed live that this was a narrow mislabel, not the same class of problem: Elgin's atom_did values are real (e.g. elgin_tx/elgin-code-of-ordinances-current-supplement/46-233 resolves to a real ingested atom whose bodyText contains the exact cited quote, spot-checked directly). Relabeled to 'asserted'.

criticalCorrectionToTheOriginalPremise: The task was framed as 'no code-section atom corpus exists yet for any city, confirmed universal.' Live-verified this is false before designing anything: queried the real atoms store (hauska_mcp, entity_type='code-section') directly. belton_tx, waco_tx, seguin_tx, and cibolo_tx are genuinely zero -- the new state is correctly targeted at these. But killeen_tx (637 atoms), elgin_tx (266 atoms), and round_rock_tx (361 atoms) already have real, non-trivial code-section corpora. cente-67 followed up on Round Rock specifically and found a further nuance: even with a corrected atom_did, Round Rock's real ingested bodyText for the cited sections doesn't contain the actual numeric dimensional-standards chart content (a table-extraction gap, not corpus absence) -- so atom count alone does not guarantee a citation can actually round-trip; per-section bodyText content has to be checked too. This same care needs to be applied to Killeen before assuming its 637 atoms make real atom-backed citations achievable there.
openFollowUps: Killeen: still needs a decision on whether its real citations can round-trip against its actual 637-atom corpus (per-section bodyText check, same method cente-67 used for Round Rock) before choosing between real atom-backed citations vs. the new primary-source-verified state. Not resolved by this PR.

hauska-engine's own Waco/Round Rock/Kyle setback files: cente-67 (Engine) is applying the equivalent relabel there once this PR landed (pinged them at merge). Round Rock specifically needs the Round-Rock-style table-extraction-gap treatment, not a blanket zero-corpus relabel.

Elgin: a full per-field G5 round-trip verification (promoting qualifying fields from 'asserted' to 'human-verified') was not done here -- only one field was spot-checked. Reasonable follow-up, not urgent (asserted is safe and valid as shipped).
testing: 23 tests in setbackGate.test.ts (16 existing + 7 new). Full lib/adapters suite: 391 passing. lib/cad-ingest unaffected: 288 passing. tsc --build clean on both packages. CI green (Test job 12m43s).
